description: iter7 + ships head: class-weighted CE (β=0.9999) + ordinal-aware label smoothing (α=0.1).

training.ships_weights_note: β=0.9999 produces near-uniform weights for ships (14% vs 66% split). Minority bucket 2 gets only +0.02x. Real rebalancing pressure here is ordinal smoothing, not class weight.

conclusion: Ships ordinal smoothing (α=0.1) was net-negative at the val level — bucket 2 F1 dropped from 0.267→0.219 and bucket 3 over-prediction worsened. Hypothesis: when gt bucket 3 is 66% majority, leaking α mass to neighbouring bucket 2 at every bucket-3 true label creates a regression pressure that outweighs the upside on true-bucket-2 samples. Also, β=0.9999 produces near-uniform ships weights (1.13/0.96/0.96/0.95) which provides negligible rebalancing on its own.
decision: Do NOT adopt iter8. Rather than iter8b (tune α lower + β=0.999), pivot to Phase 2-4 (from head). Rationale: iter7 target improvement (+10% macro_f1) did not translate to win rate — suggests from_head gating is the tactical bottleneck. Fix the ship deciding WHETHER to fire before tuning what ships it fires.
